transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has landed in Miami.
He's flown through several countries ever since losing the presidential election last
Sunday to incumbent Luis Ignacio Lula da Silva.
The Trump administration says it will provide Bolsonaro and his family with visas.
Spanish authorities have increased the death toll from a train crash today to at least
64 people.
One train collided with the second that was stopped.
It's not clear why the second train was stationary.
Spanish officials are suggesting human error may be the reason.
President Trump heads for Chillicothe, Ohio today to campaign for Republicans, and Pierce
Danielle Kurtzleben says Trump has been focusing on GOP-led states to motivate Republicans
to vote.
"The case for these rallies is simple.
It's that Trump is still really, really good at energizing the base.
And the GOP base still loves him, so the theory is that there are still gettable MAGA votes
to turn out.
Now all that said, it is still true Trump is showing up in red states to do this.
So if he needs, and that's if, to get extra votes in a red state, that still signals a
problem for his party."
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reporting.
The filing system for the Federal Election Commission remains offline this morning.
There's less than a week to go before election day.
Federal officials say they're investigating what's happened, as NPR's Ashley Lopez reports.
The FEC is an independent agency that regulates campaign finances in elections.
It does not play any role in administering elections, though.
So this outage does not affect any of voters' ability to cast a ballot.
However, the agency does keep record of how much money campaigns are raising and spending,
especially this last week of voting, which has the highest spending days for campaigns.
According to the FEC, campaigns are currently unable to use online web forms like the Electronic
Filing System for Campaign Finance reports.
The broader FEC website, however, is currently working.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
Stocks opened higher this morning as the Commerce Department reported a widening of the U.S.
trade deficit.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 50 points in
early trading.
"The trade gap grew more than 2 percent in September, reaching nearly $135 billion.
Exports and imports were both up during the month, but imports grew faster.
Tomorrow, the Commerce Department will report on economic growth for July, August and September.
Huge investments in artificial intelligence are helping to prop up the economy, but some
of that money is flowing to computer chip makers and other suppliers outside the U.S.,
so that gets subtracted from GDP.
The Federal Reserve will announce its latest decision on interest rates this afternoon.
The central bank is widely expected to hold its benchmark rates steady today, but investors
expect the Fed to raise rates at its next meeting in December."
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
Results from yesterday's election in Israel remain too close to call.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party and the Israeli opposition are very close,
and neither have a clear path to victory.
And when Israeli officials tally which party gets the most votes, it will be a while before
a new prime minister is selected.
A meeting of the U.N. General Assembly in New York grew tense yesterday.
The U.S. ambassador traded barbs with Cuba's foreign minister.
NPR's Eder Peralta reports the U.N. body is debating the U.S. embargo on Cuba.
U.S. Ambassador to the U.N., Mike Waltz, was talking about the grandiose lives that the
Castro clan needs when Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez interrupted.
Rodriguez walked from his seat toward the podium, shouting "Point of Order."
Another Cuban diplomat shouted "Liar."
Waltz responded.
Back up, Ambassador.
Back away.
This isn't Havana.
I'm suspending the meeting.
You're not going to intimidate me.
I'm suspending the meeting.
Do you understand who you're dealing with?
Relations between the two countries are historically tense.
The U.S. has tightened sanctions and put in place an oil blockade.
On Wednesday, the U.N. General Assembly will vote on a motion condemning U.S. sanctions.
In the past, a huge majority of U.N. members have voted with Cuba.
Eder Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
The auction house Sotheby says a private buyer purchased a dinosaur fossil yesterday for
more than $47 million.
It's a smaller relative of a T-Rex.
Some scientists object.
They say this money could support museums, where fossils like these could be studied.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after flying through several countries
Spanish authorities raise death toll from train crash to at least 64 after collision with stopped train
President Trump heads to Chillicothe, Ohio to campaign for Republicans in GOP-led states
Federal Election Commission's online campaign filing system remains offline less than a week before election day
U.S. trade deficit widens in September to nearly $135 billion as imports outpace exports
Israeli election results too close to call between Netanyahu's party and the opposition
U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz clashes with Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez at U.N. General Assembly
